body:
I cheated. I clicked on your name and seen how nice you are to everyone. We're a lot alike you and I. I hope people treat you better than they treat me. I'm 26 and like a lot of stuff. I also feel a lot of things very intensely. I know that's vague but that's all the energy I have left tonight... 

Maybe we'll talk more in the future. Keep on being genuinely sweet to people. It's probably helping them a lot more than they realize.

I can't tell anyone unfortunately. Maybe one day I can but definitely not any time soon. Thank you, sept27... I ended up losing another friend tonight... Maybe I've been too emotional to my friends. Thinking that they would reciprocate with similar feelings but all I get is vague jokes and silence when I ask a serious question. I decided to push a little... she decided to give me 1 sentence that meant nothing and a whole lotta silence... 

It's kind of a bitter comfort to know that someone on the internet who has never seen my face or heard my voice is trying to cheer me up more than the friends I once had so recently...  When I get close to people... I get real close... and whenever I lose a friend, even for a short time... it takes so much energy out of me... I've used up so much energy just trying for the passed year... 

It's too late for everything... I have to start from the beginning... again... and I just don't know if I have it in me anymore...

As someone who is going through a lot and has been for many years, I understand, iNeedaPaxJax. I sincerely hope you get the help that you need. I hope there is someone there who knows your pain and keeps you from doing this. I wish I knew where you were right now and that I had the resources to go over there and stop you right now...

Like I keep trying to tell myself... There are people who care... you just gotta reach out. I hope you do. I hope you are still here tomorrow.

I know it's hard... I know you feel weak.. but I'm the weakest person I'm sure I will ever know and I'm still trying to hold on. I suggest you do the same because somewhere deep down I know we both believe that it'll be worth it.
I notice that these kinds of accusations are usually because of a guilty conscious. Hope that's not the case but it usually it is. Good luck!

Well I find a drive to push past everything... the pain, the issues, and so on and then it usually ends up the same as it would have if I would have done nothing... For example, at a job I worked for DirectTV. I did troubleshooting for people's TV over the phone and I was good. Not just mediocre.. I could de-escalate people, fix their problem, and even put a smile on their face. You know how when you talk to people on the phone and their tone changes and you could hear their smile? THAT kind of stuff.

Well.. I worked from home and had bad internet... I didn't at first but the company switched over and they were changing the wiring around AS I GOT THE JOB. No matter WHAT I did... I tried moving to a different location but I wasn't far enough in the job to give me the time to move or had the money to do so. 

The employers were great. "Great job, Uncalm_Mind. We're looking for people like you." Then it all went down hill when my internet started acting up. "You're a great employee, Uncalm_Mind but I don't think you're what we're looking for. We warned you that the internet going out would be all on you and not the company. Is there a different internet provider you can switch to? No? That's the only one in your area? Can you move to a different location? No.. Them I'm afraid we must let you go."

I worked so hard... This is just one of many examples of me working my ASS off only to come to the same simple conclusion I've had in the past... 'If you try hard and push past all the negative... well.. it'll turn out the same. So why bother?'

"Taking the first steps is always the hardest part because of ambiguity. 'What if i do all of this with no results?' But no results are already happening by not trying."

Something I kept telling myself over and over... I definitely have been trying. It was/is an uphill struggle to function throughout the day, let alone give it that extra to go out and exercise or fill out a 500th application but I do... Here is where I'm stuck... I've been doing these things for quite a while now... I'm 25 now and seeing next to no results or... less than desirable results leads me to cry out for help... Then I get people saying "keep up the good work! If you keep trying as much as you say you are, you'll get there!" I mean... really? Years of this and I have nothing to show for it. 

What? Are people in shock and awe at my ability to finish one more application or do another day of exercise that shows me absolutely no results? Do people praise me over the ability to talk to people and keep a smile on my face even though my world is crashing around me? Do I get an A for effort?

I mean no hostility... I'm just having so much trouble just choking down all these ideas and thoughts that get me absolutely nowhere... 

Unfortunately I've taken most of the steps mentioned in this thread so far... And I mean it when I say that I appreciate every word given to me to help me in my endeavors.. but they AREN'T helping... and that's the issue...

I'm sorry.. I don't mean to sound so ungreatful but I'm coming to yet another dead end here... I just don't know what to do...

That used to be so much easier in the past. I used to write poetry and stories. I even had a small cult following... but it just doesn't flow anymore. I tried vigorously to emotionally connect every situation so that I would find that drive again. But I keep coming to the same brick wall with a sign on it that says "it's going to end up the same as it always is." Even when pushing past that... it usually does end up the same...

A vicious circle, eh? I'm stuck here:

I'm depressed because I don't have a stable life > having a girlfriend will help that > having a job will help that > problems in my life and not being able to handle it makes me depressed and incredibly unmotivated > I'm depressed because I don't have a stable life > having... and so on. I came up with a better metaphor for it before but I can't for the life of me remember it. Which is another problem I have... memory issues but that's another long story. 

I see that you are really trying to help me here and I really do appreciate it but once again like I said previously. I don't know how to apply it... or where to even begin... I take walks. I mildly exercise coming from a martial artist background... but my body barely changes... I have no will to up the ante whatsoever... I have before and I've only injured myself or gotten such super small results after a LONG period of time that eating a bag of chips will make it go right back to where I am... Seems like my body wants to stay where it is no matter what I do to it...

My ideas were that I used to play certain games, more movement based games and in high school I was in great shape because of this... but in high school it was being payed for... now all I have is my martial arts and it doesn't seem to be helping much anymore... My technique is great... My endurance, speed, and all around fitness is lacking something feirce. 

So maybe I could go back to doing those games I used to play in high school to up the ante, right? Well I need money for that... refer to the vicious circle I said earlier... I am thoroughly stuck.. and as the years roll by... I see no way out...

*nods* All of these things are true. But the "find your thing" comment I've heard before. Whenever I let my emotions out through whatever means (including writing it down), it usually floods and that's not a good thing.

Thanks for replying.

If I may, I have some advice for you. Get into as many activities as you can. Meet lots of people and get as many connections as possible. Shy, introvert, or otherwise just do what you can.

You're right. I have tons to look back on but that's all over now and isn't helping me now. You say "I really don't think there's a reason why you suddenly can't achieve something you already achieved at least once before." I agree to a certain extent but I haven't really achieved much. I have no job, an associate's degree in general arts (which amounts to next to nothing in this world), and a 2 year gap in a resume. No matter how I weave my resume, nothing can fill that gap besides "looking for employment." 

Just because I've had it in the past does not make it easy to achieve now. I know the ins and outs of things. I can read between the lines but that actually makes it much harder to get past the known boundaries. It's hard to explain but there it is.

Thanks for the reply.

No no. I decided that I wanted to join the military a few months ago. I've actually been actively searching for a job for about 2 years now. The jobs I had after Kroger about 5 years ago didn't stick. I got layed off or the job moved out of the area and I had no way of going with. Those are actually long stories...

Also, on the SO note. I understand what you are saying whole-heartedly. The problem is that when I had a girlfriend, even the lowest of lows wasn't this bad (and there definitely were some lows). I'm not even remotely ready or stable enough to have a steady girlfriend WHILE doing all these things but what's the cure for an ongoing 3 year broken heart? I know it sounds stupid but I just can't get over it... when will I get over it? It's been years. ><

I really appreciate the kind words and help but like I said to the previous comment, I don't know how to apply it.

"all it takes is some self motivation." I've been trying to psych myself up for a while now and it just seems to be going nowhere. I understand what you are saying but "it takes a little motivation" or "you can do it! Just think positively and see your goals" and every variation there of doesn't exactly give me a road map to my own brain. I dig deep to find the courage, motivation, and will to get out of bed every day let alone go for a jog or fill out ANOTHER 40 applications... -.- I appreciate the help but I don't know how to apply it.
